questions.q: Report: She said, 'I will finish the project tomorrow.'
questions.a: 'She said (that) she would finish the project the next day.' will→would, I→she, tomorrow→the next day. A wrong answer keeping 'will' or 'tomorrow' reveals the student did a partial transform — verb only — missing that reported speech re-anchors ALL pointing words, not just the verb.

questions.q: Report: 'The earth is round,' the teacher said.
questions.a: 'The teacher said (that) the earth is round' — universal truths keep present tense. A wrong answer 'was round' reveals over-shifting: the student applied the table mechanically without the truth-exemption — the classic competent-but-rigid error boards love to test.

questions.q: Report: He said, 'I saw this film here yesterday.'
questions.a: 'He said he had seen that film there the day before.' saw→had seen (past→past perfect), this→that, here→there, yesterday→the day before. A wrong answer 'he saw that film here yesterday' shows the student backshifted nothing but pronouns — the deictic field is invisible to them.

questions.q: ______ speech moves every tense one step back: present→past, past→past perfect, will→would, can→could, am/is→was, have→had.
Fill in the blank: ______ speech moves every tense one step back: present→past, past→past perfect, will→would, can→could, am/is→was, have→had.

Fill in the blank: Build the machine visibly: Direct 'I am tired today' → Reported 'She said (that) she was tired that day.' Highlight every change: I→she (speaker re-anchor), am→was (______), today→that day (deictic shift).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student converts statements, questions, and commands between direct and indirect speech with correct backshift, pronoun re-anchoring, and time/place expression changes, in both directions.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Build the machine visibly: Direct 'I am tired today' → Reported 'She said (that) she was tired that day.' ______ every change: I→she (speaker re-anchor), am→was (backshift), today→that day (deictic shift).
